rows.anchor: or no report exists; `--outcome succeeded` otherwise, including `partial`
rows.finding: WC-5 sends succeeded for any existing report that does not say failed or blocked; it must send succeeded only when status parses as succeeded or partial.
rows.label: N1 WC-5 empty or unparseable report maps to succeeded
rows.wrong_outcome: A report that exists but is empty, truncated, has no status, or uses the legacy value success is mapped to --outcome succeeded, so Orca settles a failed Task as done.

rows.anchor: No single tool call a command makes may block the session for longer than 240 s
rows.finding: WC-10 must say whether Agent-tool subagent calls are exempt from the 240 s single-call limit, and AC-4.3 must measure the same thing.
rows.label: N2 240 s limit vs Agent-tool calls ambiguous
rows.wrong_outcome: Read literally, every fan-out command (adversarial, troubleshoot Tier 2) breaks WC-10 and AC-4.3 fails pr-submit whenever its evidence-validator subagent runs over 4 minutes; read the other way, the limit has an unstated exemption.

rows.anchor: For each Task the coordinator's brief states:
rows.finding: WC-10 and WC-3 each call their item one more item of the section 2.3 list, but the list names only command line, output directory, outward actions and placement.
rows.label: N3 section 2.3 brief list omits run-time budget and question-answer item
rows.wrong_outcome: A coordinator following section 2.3 sends no run-time budget, so WC-10's escalation bound has no value and a stuck subagent is never escalated; it also omits whether questions are answered.

rows.anchor: A command either resumes from its on-disk state when given its resume flag
rows.finding: The start-of-attempt overwrite applies only to commands without a resume flag; it must apply to resumed attempts too.
rows.label: N4 WC-6 stale-report guard misses resuming commands
rows.wrong_outcome: An implicit-resume retry (implement) that dies before its final write leaves the earlier blocked report and its already-answered question at the recorded path, read as the retry's result.

rows.finding: AC-2.2 and WC-3 (R21) require every P2 gate-trigger run to end failed and blocked, but several P2 rows resolve their gate by a documented default.
rows.label: N5 AC-2.2 expects blocked for default-resolved gates
rows.wrong_outcome: A correct /sc:auggie-review --unattended run that skips posting and succeeds fails AC-2.2, as do cleanup, improve, research, tasklist and reflect gates that resolve by a default.

rows.anchor: 7.2 live check on each P1 command with `--unattended --output <dir>`
rows.finding: AC-1.2 must use each command's WC-4a report flag and name which commands are P1 commands.
rows.label: N6 AC-1.2 passes --output to every P1 command
rows.wrong_outcome: AC-1.2 run as written on workflow stops with E-LEGACY before any package or report exists, failing a correct implementation; index-repo, cleanup-audit and --report-dir commands get the wrong flag too.

rows.anchor: none: use it as a step inside another worker's brief, not as its own Task
rows.finding: P1 makes every 3.1-3.2 command accept --unattended, WC-4 makes unattended runs write a report, and AC-1.1 requires a section naming return-contract.yaml, while the load row says it writes no report.
rows.label: N7 load gets --unattended and an Unattended section but writes no report
rows.wrong_outcome: AC-1.1 fails on the correct usage-line-only load change, or load's Unattended section claims a return-contract.yaml it never writes; load's behaviour under --unattended is undefined.

rows.anchor: Stage 10.5 passes `--unattended` to each reflect so the headless rule applies
rows.finding: Stage 10.5 fans out one reflect --remediate agent per phase in parallel; with the headless rule each authors a corrective plan through sc:workflow.
rows.label: N8 tasklist --unattended runs N parallel reflect remediations in one worktree
rows.wrong_outcome: N parallel reflect agents auto-author workflow packages that stage .dev/tasks in one worktree, which the spec forbids for workers, and the new packages are not in tasklist's report, so 7.2 step 6 fails.

rows.finding: AC-C5 says AC-0.3 uses the --numstat test instead of its grep, but the AC-0.3 row still prints the grep that misses a deleted Markdown bullet.
rows.label: N9 AC-0.3 row still uses the replaced grep

rows.anchor: the repo itself treats it as unproven until a recorded smoke check shows it
rows.finding: The cited ~/.claude/commands/sc/spec-panel-ledger.md has no source copy in src/superclaude/commands/, so it is not the repo's statement.
rows.label: N10 WC-10 attributes an installed file to the repo

rows.anchor: need the user's authorization in this repo
rows.finding: .dev/orca-command-refactor/README.md:31 is this run's worker rule, not a repo-wide authorization rule; the verdict stands on the other citations.
rows.label: N11 git row cites a run rule as a repo rule

rows.anchor: has a `## Unattended mode` section naming `return-contract.yaml` and `~/.claude/WORKER-CONTRACT.md`
rows.finding: For adversarial, brainstorm, reflect, workflow and troubleshoot the WC-4 report is worker-contract.yaml; AC-1.1 must assert the WC-4a filename per command.
rows.label: N12 AC-1.1 asserts return-contract.yaml where WC-4a requires worker-contract.yaml
rows.wrong_outcome: A brainstorm Unattended section that points the worker at the legacy return-contract.yaml passes AC-1.1, and no P1 live check covers brainstorm, so the wrong report path reaches P2.
